name: Cobalt
brand: Says: we are the layer underneath, not the shiny thing on top. Stripe, Linear and Plaid all live here for the same reason — blue is what software looks like when it wants to be trusted with something important.
market: The safest choice against Goyzer and Reapit, and the most crowded. You will not be remembered for it, but you will never be doubted because of it. In a room with a compliance-minded owner, that is worth more than distinctiveness.
psych: Blue lowers arousal and reads as competence rather than excitement. In studies of colour and trust it consistently rates highest for reliability. The trade-off is that it is emotionally cool — nobody loves a blue brand.
risk: Invisible. Every second B2B tool is this colour.

name: Pine
brand: Green is WhatsApp, and we live inside WhatsApp. This is the only palette that makes the product feel like a natural extension of the thing the agent already has open, rather than a separate system bolted alongside it.
market: Bayut is green. That cuts both ways: it is the visual language of UAE property already, so it reads as belonging — but it also risks reading as a portal rather than the system of record. Deeper and less saturated than Bayut solves most of that.
psych: Green signals growth, permission and safety. In an interface it means 'go' — which is exactly right for a product whose entire promise is that things keep moving while you sleep.
risk: Reads as portal-adjacent. Must sit well away from Bayut's brighter green.

name: Deep teal
brand: Blue's seriousness with green's reassurance, and neither one's baggage. It is the colour of things that handle money carefully — Wise, Xero and most of European fintech sit in this family.
market: Distinctive in UAE property without being loud. Nobody in this specific market owns it, which is rare for a colour this safe. It photographs well on a phone screen, which matters more than it sounds.
psych: Sits at the calmest point on the arousal scale while still reading as active. It is the colour people describe as 'clean' — which is the exact quality you want attached to a system holding a client list.
risk: Slightly clinical. Needs warm neutrals around it or it goes cold.

name: Amber
brand: Warmth, and a deliberate rejection of the blue-grey sea. This is the only palette that feels like a person rather than a system, which matters when the product's whole job is to sound human at eleven at night.
market: Genuinely differentiated. In a category where everything is blue, warm is memorable — and memorable is what you need when a brokerage owner is describing you to a partner three days after the meeting.
psych: Amber raises attention without the threat response red triggers. It is associated with light and lamps — the connotation is being switched on when everything else is dark, which is almost embarrassingly on-brief.
risk: Warm accents fight photographs of property. Needs discipline in how imagery is treated.

name: Graphite
brand: The most confident option and the hardest to execute. Contrast is the accent — a near-black button on near-white. It says the product does not need a colour to be interesting, which is either true or very obviously not.
market: Reads premium and slightly severe. It is what a category leader does after it has stopped trying to be noticed. For a pre-launch product it is a claim you have not yet earned, which is the argument against it.
psych: Absence of hue removes emotional cueing entirely and leaves only hierarchy. People read it as serious and expensive. It also removes your ability to use colour to guide attention, so every affordance has to be carried by typography and space.
risk: No colour to signal state. Error, success and pending all have to be shape and words.
